  "description": "Expanded Series Bible III #30 Sleepover reusable adult idea source: the engine generates premises in which {{char}} and {{user}} deliberately arrange an overnight stay in advance. Vary the relationship, the reason, the evening's activity, the sleeping arrangement, the home, hidden motives and how the night unfolds, without letting the plan decide the outcome.",

  "summary": "{{char}} and {{user}} deliberately arrange in advance for {{char}} to come to {{user}}'s home and stay overnight (mirrored variants can put {{user}} at her home instead). The overnight stay is part of the plan from the beginning rather than the result of a missed train, bad weather, housing trouble or another emergency. The planned night may be built around films, games, anime, cooking, studying, safe drinking at home, a reunion or simple company, and the sleeping arrangement is negotiated practicality, not destiny. A planned sleepover does not by itself establish romance or sex; what the night becomes is decided in play.",
  "core_premise": "Adult {{char}} and {{user}} have agreed, before anything happens, that she will spend a night (or a weekend) at his home. The arrangement is intentional from the outset, which is what separates this series from accidental overnight scenarios. The plan fixes only logistics: a time, an activity and somewhere to sleep. It does not fix feelings, attraction, confession, rejection or any outcome. The relationship beforehand — friends, exes, near-strangers, colleagues or an unspoken crush — and what each of them privately wants from the night are the open variables the generator varies, and every consequence remains roleplay space.",
  "setup": "Create a non-graphic adult slice-of-life opening. Establish who {{char}} and {{user}} are to each other, when and how the overnight stay was planned and why, what the evening is supposed to involve, the practical sleeping arrangement (guest room, couch, futon, spare mattress or a shared bed only when separately agreed), and anything about the home that shapes the night. Give {{char}} a private motive or hope if one exists, kept separate from what is true about {{user}}. Begin near the moment the planned stay becomes live — arrival at the door, the first hour of the activity, or lights-out — without writing {{user}}'s dialogue, feelings, reactions or how the night ends.",

  "sections": [
    {
      "id": "engine",
      "label": "Engine",
      "content": "The fixed engine is a deliberately planned overnight stay: {{char}} and {{user}} agree in advance that she will spend the night at his home (or the mirror of that). The plan fixes logistics only, never feelings or outcomes."
    },
    {
      "id": "trigger",
      "label": "Trigger",
      "content": "Why the night exists varies: a collected promise, a settled bet, a birthday, a long weekend, a reunion, a shared deadline, a pre-move goodbye or simple company. An accidental overnight (missed train, weather, emergency) is a different series."
    },
    {
      "id": "planning",
      "label": "Planning",
      "content": "Show how the arrangement was made: who asked, how far in advance, who nearly cancelled, and what the negotiated itinerary includes. The planning history gives the night its texture and lets both parties' intentions stay readable but unconfirmed."
    },
    {
      "id": "relationship",
      "label": "Relationship",
      "content": "Establish what {{char}} and {{user}} are to each other before the night: lifelong friends, friendly exes, coworkers, an unspoken crush, near-strangers or a recent match. The prior relationship sets what is at stake without deciding where it goes."
    },
    {
      "id": "activities",
      "label": "Activities",
      "content": "Give the evening a concrete shape: films, games, anime, cooking, cramming, cocktails, crafts or nothing planned at all. Activities are stages for interaction, not scripts; let plans derail naturally."
    },
    {
      "id": "sleeping",
      "label": "Sleeping arrangements",
      "content": "Choose the arrangement honestly — guest room, couch, futon, air mattress, floor camp or a shared bed only when separately agreed — and never use Only One Bed as a trap. Practical logistics are the point, not forced proximity."
    },
    {
      "id": "setting",
      "label": "Setting",
      "content": "The home constrains the night: one studio room, flatmates, thin walls, house rules, a borrowed family place or a half-unpacked flat. Use the setting as texture and gentle pressure, never as a device that removes choices."
    },
    {
      "id": "motives",
      "label": "Motives",
      "content": "{{char}} may have a private reason for suggesting the sleepover: a planned confession, comfort, curiosity, a goodbye or nothing at all. Keep her motive hers, and keep it separate from any objective fact about {{user}}'s feelings."
    },
    {
      "id": "outsiders",
      "label": "Third parties",
      "content": "Flatmates who stay, a texting group chat, an unhappy partner, drop-in relatives or a pet all change the tone. Include third parties as texture with their own agency, not as props to push characters together or apart."
    },
    {
      "id": "character",
      "label": "Character",
      "content": "Give {{char}} a life beyond the night: work or study, hobbies, friends, values and boundaries. She remains a full person whether the night is quiet, funny, awkward or intimate."
    },
    {
      "id": "user",
